summary: Checks whether a value is an `Exception`.
description: The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is an `Exception`; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // => true
isException(new Error()); // => false
isException({}); // => false
isException(null); // => false
```
